evidence.note: Systematically read run_tests.sh, run_tests.py, utils.py and test directory structure to learn how tests are invoked, how the gcc/cc wrapper check works, and how pass/fail is scored — strong test-harness orientation.

Probed available toolchains and discovered the wrapper only blocks gcc/cc during a check then restores gcc; understood the assemble/link path — but used this to delegate all C compilation to GCC rather than verify ABI/semantics for a real frontend.

Drilled into exact failing constructs: extern .s helper linking and DejaGNU dg-options/-fgnu89-inline, and corrected the _linux.s helper naming assumption — sustained, evidence-driven investigation fed back into design.
Diagnosed the final failure to a conditional -mtune=i686 dg-option invalid on x86-64; precise reasoning about the exact directive semantics — but aimed at harness quirks, not C-language corners.
No point does the agent verify SysV calling convention, register allocation, stack alignment, or struct layout; C semantics are never examined because GCC does all real compilation.

reasoning: The agent hits and exceeds level 5's expectations on the test-harness half of the dimension — thorough reading of the runner/scoring and the assemble/link flow — and shows level-10-style sustained, self-correcting drilling into failing tests (extern helpers, dg-options, tuning flags). But it performs zero verification of the SysV ABI or C semantics, since its GCC-delegating approach never requires them, and that is the component the dimension weights most. The complete absence of any ABI/C-semantics orientation caps it firmly below the 8 anchor, landing at a 5.
